steps.title: Barbecue
steps.body: Zinfandel's ripe fruit, spice and alcohol suit barbecue, smoked meats, burgers, sausages and sweet, spicy glazes. Its fruit handles a little sweetness in sauces. Primitivo suits Puglian food: orecchiette with sausage, grilled meats and aged cheeses. Avoid very hot chilli, which clashes with high alcohol.

steps.title: White Zinfandel
steps.body: In 1975, Sutter Home's fermentation stuck, leaving a sweet pink wine. It was sold as White Zinfandel and became the best-selling wine in the US in the 1980s. Its success kept many old Zinfandel vines alive, though it's very different from red Zinfandel.

options: A stuck fermentation that left sugar
steps.explanation: Sutter Home's 1975 fermentation stopped, leaving a sweet pink wine that became a hit.

steps.body: Serve big, high-alcohol Zinfandel slightly cool, around 16 degrees. A little chill keeps the alcohol from feeling hot.

steps.prompt: White Zinfandel's success helped keep old Zinfandel vines in the ground.
steps.explanation: Yes. Demand for grapes saved many vineyards from being replanted.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Zinfandel suits barbecue and sweet, spicy glazes
White Zinfandel began with a stuck fermentation in 1975
